voiceover: Did Jesus ever actually say he was God? One of the strongest answers doesn't start with John's famous 'I am' sayings. It starts with Mark, the earliest Gospel, and the reaction of Jesus' own enemies. Scene one. Mark chapter two: a paralyzed man is lowered through a roof, and Jesus tells him his sins are forgiven. The religious scholars are stunned. 'Who can forgive sins,' they say, 'but God alone?' Forgiving sins was God's own prerogative — and Jesus had just claimed it. Scene two. Mark chapter fourteen: on trial for his life, the high priest asks, 'Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?' Jesus answers in the words of Daniel and the Psalms: the Son of Man, seated at the right hand of Power, coming with the clouds of heaven. The high priest tears his robes and cries blasphemy. Authority to forgive on earth, and authority to judge from heaven — a place that belongs to God alone. Jesus never needed the words 'I am God.' His enemies understood exactly what he was claiming. He claimed it from the start.
